script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for November 29. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Who gets to decide?  In autocracy, one person.  In oligarchy, a few.

Democracy isn't just elections. It includes free speech, free press, independent courts, peaceful assembly. These elements together create democratic society. Voting without these is hollow. Democracy requires informed citizens.  When people don't know issues, democracy degrades.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: When affected people participate in decisions, outcomes better reflect collective needs.  Value the messy process of deciding together.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Democratic Practice - How Do You Participate?.

Here's your activity: Beyond voting, how do you participate in democracy? Do you stay informed, speak up, contact representatives, attend meetings? Choose one way to strengthen your democratic participation. This helps you strengthen democratic engagement.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about people deciding together can be applied to democratic practice - how do you participate?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
